tagline: Three miles of the old Boston Turnpike into Pomfret Center.
intro: Route 244 is the Boston Turnpike, and the scenic part runs east from Ragged Hill Road to its end at Route 97 in Pomfret Center.

This was once part of the Middle Boston Post Road, one of the principal roads from Hartford to Boston and Providence. It opened as a private toll road in 1797 and went back to being a public road in 1879. The state only gave it a posted number in 1988.

moments.title: Bara-Hack
moments.text: Settled in 1778 by two families fleeing the British in Rhode Island, the spinning-wheel hamlet was abandoned by 1890 and is now stone foundations under forest on private property.

moments.title: Pomfret Center
moments.text: The turnpike runs beside the Vineyard Valley Golf Club and ends at Route 97, which carries the road on north toward US 44 and Route 169.
